the magnitude of hyoid and leryngeal movements during swallow is scaled by the initial upper airway size, such that individuals increase laryngeal elevations in response to increased upper airway opening.
the human swallowing mechanism adapts to upper airway protection needs by scaling hyoid and larryngeal movements during deglutition.
hyoid and lumenaryngeal movements scale to upper airway area, and that individuals increase laryngeal movement in response to increased upper airway area.

the mechanisms underlying the regulation of swallowing and the role of swallowing in the maintenance of health.
how the brain controls swallowing and how the brain adapts swallowing to changes in upper airway size.
